response.title: how long should a battery backup last
response.answer:
If you're referring to a UPS (Uninterruptible Power Supply) battery backup for a computer, router, or other electronics, there are two ways to measure how long it should last.

1. Runtime during a power outage

Device connected

	

Typical backup runtime




Wi-Fi router (10–20W)

	

2–8 hours




Laptop (30–60W)

	

1–3 hours




Desktop PC (150–300W)

	

10–30 minutes




Gaming PC (400–700W)

	

3–15 minutes




Server (300–600W)

	

5–20 minutes

These are rough estimates for common consumer UPS units (600–1500VA). Actual runtime depends heavily on battery capacity and power consumption.

2. Battery lifespan before replacement

Typical UPS battery: 3–5 years

High-quality lead-acid battery: 4–6 years under favorable conditions

Lithium-ion UPS battery: 8–10 years or longer

Heat, frequent power outages, and deep discharges can shorten battery life.

How many years a battery backup should last before needing replacement?

Also, what brand/model do you have (APC, CyberPower, etc.)? I can give you a more specific estimate.

### 1. Runtime during a power outage

| Device connected | Typical backup runtime |
|---|---|
| Wi-Fi router (10–20W) | 2–8 hours |
| Laptop (30–60W) | 1–3 hours |
| Desktop PC (150–300W) | 10–30 minutes |
| Gaming PC (400–700W) | 3–15 minutes |
| Server (300–600W) | 5–20 minutes |

These are rough estimates for common consumer UPS units (600–1500VA). Actual runtime depends heavily on battery capacity and power consumption.

### 2. Battery lifespan before replacement

- **Typical UPS battery:** 3–5 years
- **High-quality lead-acid battery:** 4–6 years under favorable conditions
- **Lithium-ion UPS battery:** 8–10 years or longer

Heat, frequent power outages, and deep discharges can shorten battery life.
